subject.title: fix(security): ignore string-literal contents in code-safety env/exfil rules (#82469)

question: Should OpenClaw accept env-harvesting-only string-literal masking, including the documented non-recursive nested-template residual, as the scanner boundary for this bug fix?
rationale: The patch reduces critical false positives without reducing file coverage, but it changes how a security audit heuristic sees source syntax and final acceptance of that boundary belongs to a security owner.

options.title: Accept env-harvesting-only masking
options.body: Keep potential-exfiltration and payload-matching rules unmasked, accept the documented residual false-positive edge, and proceed after normal CI and owner review.

options.title: Require parser-backed masking
options.body: Pause the heuristic lexer and require a syntax-aware tokenizer or parser before changing security-audit behavior.

options.title: Narrow the repair
options.body: Replace the broader masking helper with a smaller context-rule change if maintainers prefer less scanner surface at the cost of less complete false-positive cleanup.

recommendation.title: Accept env-harvesting-only masking
recommendation.body: Keep potential-exfiltration and payload-matching rules unmasked, accept the documented residual false-positive edge, and proceed after normal CI and owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the clearest security/scanner routing candidate from CONTRIBUTING.md and recent scanner-path history.
